title: Activation Orbit - 30/60/90 Onboarding & Adoption Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, tactical playbook for Customer Success managers running the first 90 days post-contract for SMB and mid-market customers. The 'Activation Orbit' approach centers on measurable early value, predictable content handoffs, and explicit renewal signals into M+6.

Context and assumptions:
- Target accounts: SMB / low-touch mid-market (initial ARR under $200k).
- Product scope: Redwood hosted API + optional Redwood Optimize onboarding.
- Typical kickoff within 7 days of PO signature.
- Primary goal: reach "activated" state (customer running production inference with 1+ route and observed latency < target) within 90 days.

High-level success metrics (north star and leading indicators):
- North star: First-value events/month (calls that convert testers → internal adopters).
- Leading indicators (week-by-week focus):
  - Week 1–2: Kickoff complete, integration environment provisioned, test tokens used.
  - Week 3–4: Baseline throughput test, first inference calls logged, basic observability connected.
  - Week 5–8: Cost/latency profile identified, caching/batching recommendations implemented.
  - Week 9–12: Production route live, automated alerts configured, success criteria validated.
- Renewal signal score (tracked as scorecard): product usage, latency SLO attainment, number of active routes, stakeholder engagement (weekly cadence kept).

Stakeholder map (templates):
- CSM (owner): onboarding project manager, weekly check-ins, renewal owner at month 6.
- Customer engineering lead: integration owner, API keys and security signoff.
- Product manager (customer side): prioritization contact for custom needs.
- Procurement/legal: billing / contract questions.

30/60/90 milestones (Activation Orbit cadence) — responsibilities and artifacts:
- Days 0–30 (Orbit Insertion) — outcomes: kickoff, sandbox calls, integration proof-of-life.
  - Deliverables: kickoff notes, sandbox usage checklist, initial metrics dashboard.
  - CSM actions: schedule technical kickoff, confirm API access and allowed IPs, run baseline smoke tests with customer sample prompts.
  - Engineering actions: provision test capacity, validate tokens, provide sample SDK snippets.
  - Customer success signals: first 100 inference calls, console telemetry visible.

- Days 31–60 (Orbit Stabilize) — outcomes: repeatable latency/cost baseline, early optimization experiments.
  - Deliverables: cost/latency heatmap, caching/batching recommendation doc, one optimization experiment executed.
  - CSM actions: review heatmap with customer, advise on Redwood Optimize suggestions, coordinate a joint runbook for error handling.
  - Engineering actions: help implement recommended batch sizes/quant profiles, verify metrics collection in Console.
  - Customer success signals: 3x week active usage, alerts firing for threshold breaches (simulated or real).

- Days 61–90 (Orbit Burn-in) — outcomes: production route(s) live, SLOs and alerting in place, internal team trained.
  - Deliverables: production cutover checklist, training session slide deck, acceptance signoff.
  - CSM actions: execute handoff checklist, collect acceptance signoff (email), schedule renewal planning intro (M+6).
  - Engineering actions: finalize autoscaling policy, validate fallback policies and canary rollout settings.
  - Customer success signals: sustained usage > threshold for 7 consecutive days, cost per 1k tokens within expected range, no critical incidents in last 14 days.

Risk register (quick reference):
- No API calls in week 1: root causes (no credentials, internal blockers) — mitigation: daily async check-ins, technical office hours slot.
- Cost shock after scale test: mitigation: apply hard quota, suggest deduplication/caching, pause noncritical routes.
- Latency outliers during load: mitigation: enable prefix caching, temporary routing to dedicated capacity or smaller model variant for non-critical traffic.

Playbook triggers and automated nudges (recommended automations):
- Trigger: 0 calls by day 7 → Automated Slack DM to CSM + templated troubleshooting checklist to customer.
- Trigger: cost > 2x expected in week 1 → Auto email to CSM and finance contact with cost breakdown.
- Trigger: SLO breaches 3x in 24h → Pager to SRE on-call and optional automated rollback to previous model version.

Email templates (short, editable):
- Kickoff invite: "Hi <Customer>, excited to kick off—proposed agenda: intros, success criteria, integration plan, next steps. Please share API owner and IP allowlist by [date]."
- 30-day health email: "Quick update: baseline metrics attached; we recommend enabling batching and a 128-token cache for route X—planning time?"
- 90-day acceptance: "Congrats—production route validated. Please reply with acceptance to start renewal conversations and optional Dedicated capacity trial."

Simple checklists (CSM use):
- Pre-kickoff checklist: Po signed, billing verified, API keys created, test dataset received, internal Slack + calendar invites set.
- Cutover checklist: smoke test pass, alerts active, policy docs shared, internal runbook created, stakeholder acceptance recorded.

Renewal signals & M+6 handoff play (short):
- Signal thresholds to kick sales/renewal outreach: usage >= 60% of tier capacity, <2 critical incidents/month, NPS >= +6 from product survey.
- Handoff packet contents: 90-day success metrics, sample invoices, roadmap requests, risk items and mitigation history, proposed renewal tier and recommended Dedicated options.

Lightweight dashboards to share (one-pager):
- Week-over-week calls, average latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, number of active routes, SLO compliance %.

Notes to self / known TODOs (incomplete ideas):
- Build a short automated survey at day 45 for friction signals (2 questions + free text).
- Add a quick integration map template (customer architecture + where Redwood routes live).
- Consider a low-touch 'activation bot' that runs the pre-kickoff checklist and pings the API owner automatically.

Links & refs (internal):
- Similar playbook (engineering-facing): CONFLUENCE-ENG-420 — use for detailed runbook steps.
- Template repo: github.com/redwood-inference/customer-templates (copy onboarding deck there).

Appendix: example acceptance criteria checklist (CSM presents):
- API keys validated in customer prod account.
- Console shows stable telemetry for 7 days.
- Latency p95 within agreed SLO or documented exception.
- Alerts and escalation paths confirmed.
- Stakeholder acceptance email present.

If this reads useful, next steps: iterate with Solutions Eng on the heatmap format, create the day-45 survey, and wire the three automations into our internal Slackbot.

End of doc.
